newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico employers' chief sees November Pacto.
newsitem.headline: Mexico employers' chief sees November Pacto.

text.p: The president of Mexico's employers' federation Coparmex dismissed pressure from labour groups to bring forward a new economic pact between the government, labor and business, saying he expected a new Pacto for 1997 to be signed in November, as is traditional.

"The sectors who take part in the Alliance agree that we should give the new negotiations as much space as possible... we calmly see the renewal of the Alliance in the month of November, probably," Coparmex chief Carlos Abascal told Reuters in an interview late on Friday.
The annual tripartite accord, signed in November last year to cover 1996, is formally known as the Alliance for Economic Recovery and informally as the Pacto.

"With all objectivity, the pressure is totally artificial," Abascal said. "Of course there are some trade union leaders talking about this, but the consensus in the Alliance is that there is no such pressure."

Abascal was referring, among others, to a dissident group within the teachers' union, which has asked for a 56 percent wage increase in 1997 -- well above any minimum wage rise the Alliance is likely to agree.
"What worries me is that an artificial climate of this kind hurts the markets, the economy, and the people who are worst hurt are the poorest," Abascal added.
